After dark on Saturday nights, the young people of the Midwestern town gathered at the country club, where the girls danced and the boys took turns cutting in. <break time="0.8s" /> Watching from the edge of the floor, the older women judged each dancer, and they knew exactly which girls were popular and which girls were not. <break time="0.8s" /> Warren McIntyre, a Yale student who was home for the summer, had loved Marjorie Harvey for years, but she gave him little attention in return. <break time="0.8s" /> This August, Marjories cousin Bernice had come from Eau Claire to visit, and Marjorie expected the boys to entertain her guest at every dance. <break time="0.8s" /> As a favor to Marjorie, Warren danced with Bernice that night, but the pretty, polite girl offered him nothing except a few dull remarks. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice was beautiful enough, yet she had no idea how to amuse a young man, and her partners soon began to look around the room desperately. <break time="0.8s" /> No boy wanted to be stuck with her for long, so each one waited anxiously for a friend who might cut in and rescue him. <break time="0.8s" /> Marjorie, on the other hand, was never left alone for a moment, for she knew precisely what to say and how to make every boy laugh.
